description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait, and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County. * WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 856 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local time): * Port Chicago: 2.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:36 AM Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue 11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26. * West Sacramento: 2.2 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 2:49 PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.4 ft at 2:00 PM Mon 11/23, +7.5 ft at 2:45 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.6 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26. - These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels are forecast hold near a crest today before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The river has surpassed its previous record flood. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:45 AM EST Monday, November 23 the stage was 13.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:45 AM AM EST Monday was 13.1 feet. - Forecast...River levels are forecast hold near a crest of 13.1 feet today before beginning a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to slowly rise mid to late week. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are inaccessible due to knee-deep water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 9:30 AM EST Monday the stage was 4.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 9:30 AM EST Monday was 4.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is forecast to slowly rise reaching 4.4 feet into late week. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
